title: Japchae
subtitle: Korean glass noodles with beef and vegetables in sesame dressing
excerpt: Japchae is a Korean celebration dish of silky glass noodles tossed with stir-fried vegetables and beef in a sweet-savoury sesame dressing. Each component is cooked separately so the flavours stay distinct. The result is light, glossy and very good.
sourceNotes: Japchae was created in Korea during the early seventeenth century as a dish for royalty. It originally contained no noodles. Sweet potato glass noodles were added later and are now the defining ingredient.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be served at room temperature and assembled up to 1 hour ahead. Add the sesame seeds just before serving.

content.text: Cook each vegetable separately in the same pan, wiping it between batches. This keeps the colours vivid and stops everything turning into one mush. The glass noodles soak up dressing quickly so do not dress them too far ahead.
Cook the glass noodles in boiling water for 6 to 8 minutes or as the packet directs. Drain, rinse with cold water and cut into roughly 15cm lengths with scissors. Transfer to a large bowl.
Mix together the soy sauce, sesame oil, honey and garlic to make the dressing. Pour two thirds of it over the noodles and toss well.
Heat a wok over high heat with a little sunflower oil. Stir-fry the beef for 2 minutes, season with a little soy, then add to the noodle bowl.
Stir-fry the carrot for 2 minutes, then the mushrooms for 3 minutes, then the spinach for 1 minute until just wilted. Add each to the bowl as you go.
Quickly stir-fry the spring onions for 1 minute, add to the bowl and pour over the remaining dressing. Toss everything together gently and serve.

items.symptom: Noodles are gluey and stuck together
items.cause: Not rinsed after cooking or left too long.
items.fix: Rinse thoroughly with cold water and toss with a little oil.

items.cause: Not enough seasoning in the dressing.
items.fix: Add more soy sauce and a few drops of sesame oil.
